extracted.intended_audience: Victims of the Takata airbag inflator matter and other members of the public seeking case and victim-rights information
extracted.subtask_description: Official Department of Justice victim-notification and case-information page for United States v. Tanaka et al. (Takata Corporation), providing procedural instructions, rights, deadlines, and resources for victims and other stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims filing deadline and claims form
rubrics_metrics.description: The court approved Special Master Green’s claims forms, notice program, and request for an extension of the current claims filing deadline. The deadline for filling out a claim form is August 31, 2018, and you can find the form here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Victims who wish to participate in restitution must complete the court-approved claims form by the deadline. The special master's forms and notice program are the authoritative submission mechanism; follow the form instructions and the special master's deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and purpose of two restitution funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Two restitution funds will be established: a $125 million fund for individuals who have been physically injured by Takata’s airbags and who have not already reached a settlement with the company, and a $850 million fund for airbag recall and replacement costs incurred by auto manufacturers who were victims of Takata’s fraud scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These funds are distinct (injury vs. recall/replacement). Eligibility and administration details will be determined and overseen by a court-appointed special master; the website will be updated with processes and procedures when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special master oversight of restitution funds
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-appointed special master will oversee administration of the restitution funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The special master is responsible for administering claims and distributing restitution according to court orders and approved procedures; victims should follow special master notices and instructions for submitting claims and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Takata criminal resolution terms and remedial obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Takata agreed to plead guilty by criminal information to one count of wire fraud and to pay a total of $1 billion in criminal penalties, including $975 million in restitution and a $25 million fine. Takata has also agreed to implement rigorous internal controls, retain a compliance monitor for a term of three years and cooperate fully with the department’s ongoing investigation, including its investigation of individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This summarizes the company's criminal commitments and remedies; victims and other stakeholders can expect restitution payments and corporate compliance measures as part of the resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of the Crime Victims’ Rights Act (18 U.S.C. § 3771)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Crime Victims’ Rights Act applies only to victims of the counts charged in federal court, and thus individuals may not be able to exercise all of these rights if the crime of which the individual is a victim was not charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a person or entity qualifies as a victim under the Act will be made by the presiding judge (Judge Steeh). Victims should understand that not all statutory rights may be available if the underlying harm was not part of the federal charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of innocence
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty and that presumption requires both the court and our office to take certain steps to ensure that justice is served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications and procedures should respect the presumption of innocence for individuals charged until conviction; this is a general principle governing the criminal process and DOJ communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to retain counsel under 18 U.S.C. § 3771(c)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3771(c)(2) requires that victims be advised they have the right to retain counsel. Although the statute specifically sets forth the right to seek advice of an attorney with regard to rights under the statute, there is no requirement that you retain counsel. The Government may not recommend any specific counsel, nor can the Government (or the Court) pay for counsel to represent you. Government attorneys represent the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you elect to obtain counsel to represent your interests, have your attorney notify the office in writing at the listed DOJ address, fax, or email (victimassistance.fraud@usdoj.gov). If you elect not to retain counsel, you do not need to do anything.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and limitations regarding plea agreements and victim notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Many criminal cases are resolved by plea agreement between the Department of Justice and the defendant. Plea agreements can be made at any time and as late as the morning of trial, leaving little or no opportunity to provide notice to you of the date and time of the plea hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the court schedules a plea hearing in this case, DOJ will use best efforts to notify victims as soon as practicable. Victims who wish to inform the prosecutor of their views regarding potential plea agreements or other aspects of the case should call the Victim Assistance Line or email the provided address to be put in touch with the prosecutor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Victim Assistance contact and notification mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For questions, victims may call the Victim Assistance Line toll-free at (888) 549-3945 or email victimassistance.fraud@usdoj.gov. If counsel is retained, the attorney should notify the office in writing at: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section, 10th & Constitution Avenue, NW, Bond Building, 4th Floor, Washington, DC 20530, Attention: Victim Witness Unit; fax: (202) 514-3708; or email: victimassistance.fraud@usdoj.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the official contact channels for victims seeking information, to convey views to prosecutors, or to register counsel so the office can coordinate notifications and rights-related processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public documents and resources for additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: The page links to related public materials for more information about the Takata and Tanaka et al. charges (Press Release – January 13, 2017; Press Release – February 27, 2017; Takata Corporation First Superseding Information; Takata Corporation Plea Agreement; Tanaka et al. Indictment; Restitution Order; Judgment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Victims and stakeholders should consult these public filings and press releases for detailed factual allegations, charging documents, plea terms, and court orders; these documents often contain the operative details relevant to rights, remedies, and timelines.
